findings.issue_text: [P1] public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:47 — The Prometheus-only list path passes `actions: <RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} groupIdentifier={groupIdentifier} compact />`, but the shared menu renders deletion only under `{canDelete && rulerRule && (` (and the silence drawer under `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`), so after removing the Ruler fetch users who are allowed by the new Prometheus ability model cannot delete or silence a Grafana-managed rule from either list.

[P2] public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rules/RulesTable.test.tsx:65 — Because the new policy path is replaced by `mocks.useGrafanaPromRuleAbility.mockReturnValue([false, false]);`, a regression in `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` for folder loading or folder-scoped edit/delete permission evaluation can ship while every altered RBAC test still passes.

[P3] public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:66 — The newly introduced recording-rule branch `if (prometheusRuleType.grafana.recordingRule(rule))` has no corresponding test, so a Prometheus-only Grafana recording rule can regress to the unknown-rule UI without any changed test detecting it.

public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx:68 — P2: Replacing the dual Ruler/Prometheus reconciliation with `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules.map` drops the former Creating/Deleting transition records, so any rollout or propagation lag between the authoritative write path and Prometheus makes recently created or deleted rules silently disappear from the list (the removed code's “strongly consistent now” assertion is the only rebuttal, not an enforced fallback).

public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/components/RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:104 — [P1, 98%] In the new Prometheus-only list path `rule` is undefined, so clicking the now-authorized Silence item only sets `showSilenceDrawer` while `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer` never mounts a drawer, leaving Silence notifications nonfunctional.

public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:165 — [P1, 98%] Prometheus-only Grafana rules can pass the new `canDelete` check, but `canDelete && rulerRule` suppresses the Delete menu item whenever the removed ruler request leaves `rulerRule` undefined, so users cannot delete rules from the list.

public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:123 — [P2, 95%] Prometheus-only Grafana rules can pass `canPause`, but `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` is false without a ruler rule and prevents `MenuItemPauseRule` from rendering, making pause/resume unavailable in the refactored list.

public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:228 — For every federated CombinedRule, routing `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` into a helper whose verbatim `const isFederated = false` disables the prior federated immutability check, so authorized users are newly offered update/delete/pause actions on rules the original behavior intentionally made immutable.

public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/components/RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:104 — On the new Prometheus-only list path, `canSilence` can expose the menu item and its `handleSilence` sets `showSilenceDrawer` true, but the verbatim `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer` can never mount the drawer when `rule` is undefined, making “Silence notifications” a silent no-op.

public/locales/en-US/grafana.json:351 — This alert-rule-list refactor also deletes unrelated ad/home promotional translations and changes the cloud badge text, expanding the change beyond the stated notification-rule processing review without a traceable requirement.

RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. This means clicking 'Silence notifications' for these rules has no visible effect, even when abilities indicate silencing is allowed.

[P2] public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rules/RulesTable.test.tsx:65 — Because the new policy path is replaced by `mocks.useGrafanaPromRuleAbility.mockReturnValue([false, false]);`, a regression in `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` for folder loading or folder-scoped edit/delete permission evaluation can ship while every altered RBAC test still passes.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a test coverage gap. The diff shows that tests mock `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` at line 65 with `mockReturnValue([false, false])` and similar patterns throughout. The new `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` hook in useAbilities.ts contains real logic including `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` which checks folder permissions via `useFolder`. Since tests mock the hook outputs directly rather than testing the actual implementation, bugs in the folder permission evaluation logic within `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` could go undetected. This is a legitimate test coverage concern for newly added nontrivial logic, though it's about test quality rather than a bug in the production code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [P3] public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:66 — The newly introduced recording-rule branch `if (prometheusRuleType.grafana.recordingRule(rule))` has no corresponding test, so a Prometheus-only Grafana recording rule can regress to the unknown-rule UI without any changed test detecting it.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx introduces a new branch for recording rules at line 66 (`if (prometheusRuleType.grafana.recordingRule(rule))`), but the test file GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx only tests alerting rules (using `rulerGroupToPromGroup(grafanaRulerGroup)` which creates alerting rules). There's no test coverage for the recording rule path in the new component. This is a valid observation about missing test coverage for newly added logic - if the recording rule type guard fails, it would silently fall through to UnknownRuleListItem without any test detecting the regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx:68 — P2: Replacing the dual Ruler/Prometheus reconciliation with `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules.map` drops the former Creating/Deleting transition records, so any rollout or propagation lag between the authoritative write path and Prometheus makes recently created or deleted rules silently disappear from the list (the removed code's “strongly consistent now” assertion is the only rebuttal, not an enforced fallback).

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the diff removes the dual Ruler/Prometheus reconciliation logic (matchRules function and the Creating/Deleting state handling). The old code in GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx showed 'Creating' state for rules that existed in Ruler but not yet in Prometheus, and 'Deleting' state for rules in Prometheus but not in Ruler. The new code only uses promResponse and removes this reconciliation entirely. However, the comment in the removed code states 'Grafana Prometheus rules should be strongly consistent now' and logs a warning when mismatches occur, suggesting this was already considered an edge case. The removal is intentional per the PR's goal to eliminate Ruler API calls. This is a legitimate architectural concern about potential UX degradation during propagation lag, but it's not a bug per se - it's a design tradeoff. The finding is valid but overstates the severity since the old code already treated mismatches as warnings rather than expected behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:165 — [P1, 98%] Prometheus-only Grafana rules can pass the new `canDelete` check, but `canDelete && rulerRule` suppresses the Delete menu item whenever the removed ruler request leaves `rulerRule` undefined, so users cannot delete rules from the list.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue. Looking at AlertRuleMenu.tsx, the diff shows that `canDelete` is now computed by combining ruler and grafana abilities (line 89-90): `canDelete = (deleteSupported && deleteAllowed) || (grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed)`. However, examining the menu rendering logic (not fully shown but referenced at line 165), the Delete menu item likely still checks `canDelete && rulerRule` as a condition. Since the PR removes ruler API requests from the list view (as stated in comments at lines 38-41), `rulerRule` will be undefined when coming from the list view. This means even when `grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed` is true (making `canDelete` true), the `&& rulerRule` check would still suppress the Delete menu item because `rulerRule` is undefined. This is a logical bug where the permission check passes but the feature gate fails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:123 — [P2, 95%] Prometheus-only Grafana rules can pass `canPause`, but `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` is false without a ruler rule and prevents `MenuItemPauseRule` from rendering, making pause/resume unavailable in the refactored list.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real bug. Looking at AlertRuleMenu.tsx, the code computes `canPause` by OR-ing ruler and grafana abilities (line 83-84). However, looking at the MenuItemPauseRule rendering condition around line 123 (not shown in full but referenced), it likely still checks `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` which would be false when only promRule exists (no rulerRule). The refactoring removes ruler API calls from the list view, meaning rulerRule will be undefined for Grafana rules in that context. While canPause would be true (from grafana abilities), the rendering condition checking rulerRule would prevent the pause menu item from appearing. This is a logical inconsistency introduced by the refactoring.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:228 — For every federated CombinedRule, routing `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` into a helper whose verbatim `const isFederated = false` disables the prior federated immutability check, so authorized users are newly offered update/delete/pause actions on rules the original behavior intentionally made immutable.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in useAllRulerRuleAbilities (lines 238-275), the code explicitly sets `const isFederated = false` with a TODO comment saying 'Add support for federated rules'. The original useAllAlertRuleAbilities function (now marked @deprecated) previously called `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` to check for federated rules. The new implementation hardcodes isFederated to false, which means federated rules will no longer be treated as immutable. This affects the `immutableRule` calculation which determines whether update/delete/pause actions are allowed. The finding correctly identifies that this change removes the federated rule immutability protection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/components/RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:104 — On the new Prometheus-only list path, `canSilence` can expose the menu item and its `handleSilence` sets `showSilenceDrawer` true, but the verbatim `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer` can never mount the drawer when `rule` is undefined, making “Silence notifications” a silent no-op.

adjudication.rationale: The finding references code at line 104 in RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx about 'rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer' controlling the SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer. However, looking at the diff, the SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer component at line 85-90 uses 'promRule' not 'rule': it checks 'rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(promRule)' and passes 'promRule' to the drawer. The component now accepts both 'rule' (RulerRuleDTO) and 'promRule' (Rule) via RequireAtLeastOne, and the silence drawer logic uses promRule. When coming from the Prometheus-only path, promRule would be provided, so the drawer can mount correctly. The finding misreads which variable controls the drawer.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims the diff deletes 'unrelated ad/home promotional translations and changes the cloud badge text'. Looking at the actual diff for public/locales/en-US/grafana.json, it only shows removal of two translation keys: 'cannot-find-rule-details-for' and 'cannot-load-rule-details-for' at lines 2402-2403. These are directly related to the GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx file that was deleted in this refactor. There is no evidence of any 'ad/home promotional translations' or 'cloud badge text' changes in the diff. The finding misreads what was actually changed in the localization file.
